# 5-Day Family Meal Plan for Toronto on 140 CAD

Nut-free, kid-friendly, and built to stretch leftovers for lunches. I’m assuming 2 adults + 2 children, standard pantry basics already on hand, and shopping at a budget grocery store in Toronto.

## 5-Day Dinner + Leftover Lunch Plan

| Day | Dinner | Lunch Plan | Est. Cost |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | Vegetarian: Veggie pasta with tomato sauce, spinach, carrots, and garlic bread | Save extra pasta for Day 2 lunches | CAD 16 |
| 2 | Chicken: Sheet-pan chicken thighs with potatoes, carrots, and broccoli | Leftover chicken + roasted vegetables in wraps or rice bowls | CAD 24 |
| 3 | Vegetarian: Bean and cheese quesadillas with corn and salsa, side salad | Extra quesadillas for lunch | CAD 14 |
| 4 | Fish: Baked fish fillets with rice, peas, and lemon-garlic green beans | Leftover fish rice bowls with veggies | CAD 26 |
| 5 | Chicken: Mild chicken stir-fry with rice, mixed vegetables, and soy-ginger sauce | Leftover stir-fry over rice | CAD 22 |

## 5-Day Meal Breakdown

### Day 1: Veggie Pasta Night
- Dinner: Pasta with tomato sauce, sautéed onion, carrots, spinach, and cheese on top
- Lunch use: Pack extra pasta for easy next-day lunches
- Kid-friendly tip: Keep the sauce mild and serve cheese on the side

### Day 2: Sheet-Pan Chicken Dinner
- Dinner: Chicken thighs roasted with potatoes, carrots, and broccoli
- Lunch use: Turn leftovers into wraps, sandwiches, or rice bowls
- Kid-friendly tip: Cut vegetables into small pieces and season lightly

### Day 3: Bean Quesadilla Night
- Dinner: Black bean and cheese quesadillas with corn and salsa
- Lunch use: Reheat leftover quesadillas for lunch
- Kid-friendly tip: Offer plain sour cream or yogurt for dipping if desired

### Day 4: Baked Fish Dinner
- Dinner: Oven-baked fish fillets with rice, peas, and green beans
- Lunch use: Flake leftover fish into rice bowls with vegetables
- Kid-friendly tip: Choose a mild fish like cod or haddock

### Day 5: Chicken Stir-Fry Night
- Dinner: Chicken stir-fry with rice and mixed vegetables in a mild soy-ginger sauce
- Lunch use: Leftover stir-fry reheats well for lunch
- Kid-friendly tip: Keep sauce light and serve extra rice for picky eaters

## Consolidated Shopping List

### Produce
- Potatoes, 5 lb bag
- Carrots, 2 lb
- Broccoli, 2 heads
- Spinach, 1 large bag
- Onions, 3 lb bag
- Garlic, 1 bulb
- Green beans, 1 lb
- Lettuce or salad mix, 1 large box
- Lemons, 2
- Mixed stir-fry vegetables, 1 large frozen bag
- Corn, 1 frozen bag or 2 cans

### Proteins
- Chicken thighs, about 3 to 3.5 kg total
- White fish fillets, about 1 to 1.2 kg
- Canned black beans, 2 cans
- Eggs, 1 dozen if you want an extra backup meal or breakfast

### Dairy
- Shredded cheese, 2 large bags
- Parmesan or pizza-style grated cheese, 1 small container
- Yogurt or sour cream, 1 tub for dipping

### Pantry
- Pasta, 2 boxes
- Rice, 2 to 3 kg bag
- Tortillas, 2 packs
- Tomato sauce or crushed tomatoes, 3 to 4 cans/jars
- Salsa, 1 jar
- Soy sauce
- Cooking oil
- Garlic powder, paprika, salt, pepper, dried Italian herbs

### Bread / Extras
- Garlic bread or 2 loaves of bread
- Optional: fruit for snacks if budget allows

## Budget Check

- Estimated total: **CAD 129 to CAD 138**
- Buffer left: **CAD 2 to CAD 11**
- Best way to stay under budget: choose store-brand pasta, rice, canned tomatoes, and frozen vegetables
